s1.syndrome_frame: pruritic skin lesions with systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory findings
salient_findings: pruritic lesions on arms and legs
right-sided headache, sinus pain, and congestion
key_facts: patient is a 75-year-old black woman
patient has insulin-dependent diabetes
patient has obesity
patient presented with a 10-day history of pruritic lesions
patient has been experiencing night sweats for 2-3 months
patient has been experiencing right-sided headache, sinus pain, and congestion for 3 weeks
skin lesions developed while patient was taking prednisone
patient has no associated fever, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, myalgia, or arthralgia
patient has dozens of 1-2 cm oedematous pink-red papules with a darker red-violet central zone
patient has about 20 red macules on the medial aspect of her feet and the tips of her fingers and toes
patient has one 2 mm erosion on the soft palate of her mouth
white blood cell count is 2.7 × 10⁹/L
haemoglobin is 100 g/L
platelet count is 129 × 10⁹/L
absolute neutrophil count is 1.4 × 10⁹/L
liver function tests are normal
urinalysis shows 2+ protein, no blood
PCR for herpes simplex virus, antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody, and cryoglobulins is negative
antinuclear antibody is <1:40
IgA levels are elevated at 8860 mg/L

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: pruritic skin lesions with vascular damage and leucocytoclasia on biopsy

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: pruritic skin lesions with systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory findings

shortlist.label: Cutaneous lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: atypical mononuclear cells on skin biopsy and abnormal localization of immature precursors on bone marrow biopsy

shortlist.label: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: elevated IgA levels and presence of atypical lymphocytes

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: pruritic skin lesions with atypical cells on biopsy and complex karyotype with chromosomal abnormalities

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of pruritic lesions, night sweats, and headache, along with the skin biopsy findings of atypical mononuclear cells and vascular damage, are consistent with Sweet syndrome. The elevated IgA levels and the presence of myeloperoxidase-positive cells also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: While the patient has vasculitis, the presence of atypical mononuclear cells and elevated IgA levels are more suggestive of Sweet syndrome.

rejected.label: Cutaneous lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's skin biopsy does not show definitive evidence of lymphoma, and the clinical presentation is more consistent with Sweet syndrome.

rejected.label: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
rejected.why: The patient's laboratory results do not show elevated IgM levels, which are characteristic of Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia.

rejected.label: Mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: The patient's skin biopsy does not show the characteristic findings of mycosis fungoides, such as epidermotropism or Pautrier's microabscesses.
